Team —

Attached is a draft exec summary for Acme QBR plus an initial SLA credit calc.
High level:
- Incident window: 2026-11-27T02:15:00Z - 2026-11-27T03:40:00Z (approx 85 minutes)
- Impact: degraded inference throughput for a subset of customer traffic using the reconciliation model (acme-prod-recon); peak 60% increased latency, 18% error rate spike.
- Customers affected: Acme Analytics (single tenant), estimated token impact: 3.8M tokens (customer-supplied job + sampling).
- Root cause (prelim): kv-cache eviction behavior + concurrent model swap under load; reproduces in internal staging when run with same sequence profiles.

Proposed remediation credits:
- SLA term: 99.9% monthly availability; estimated availability hit ~0.12% translate to credit = one week of reserved capacity prorated. See sla_credit_calc.xlsx.

Attachments:
- incident_timeline_v2.pdf (timeline, customer impact bullets)
- sla_credit_calc.xlsx (calc & assumptions)

Open items for the QBR packet:
1) Confirm final token impact figure (Jenny).
2) Confirm whether to propose a one-week credit or roll-forward credit (sales discussion).
3) Postmortem writeup (Hannah). Completion ETA: 11/30 12:00 PT.

I'll iterate on wording for the external-facing exec brief — suggest we keep it under 1 page.

-Vivek

Thanks again for flagging this and for your patience. Attached is a concise incident brief (one page), our internal timeline, and the SLA impact calc. Key points for your QBR:

- Customer impact: Acme's reconciliation job experienced increased latency and transient errors; estimated token impact: 3.8M tokens (as discussed).
- Remediation: we've merged a cache-lock fix and are scheduling a production release tomorrow AM after final verification runs.
- Credits: we propose "up to one week of reserved capacity" as a remediation credit; see attached calc. We'll finalize the exact credit after your confirmation on the token estimate.
